description: The Cityscapes dataset holds semantic, instance-wise and dense pixel annotations of street scenes recorded from a moving vehicle in 50 cities, released for research on urban scene understanding. It has 5,000 images with fine annotations and 20,000 with coarse annotations, labelled with 30 classes grouped as flat surfaces (road, sidewalk, parking, rail track), humans, vehicles, construction (building, wall, fence, bridge, tunnel), objects (poles, signs, lights), nature and sky. Metadata include the preceding and trailing video frames (each annotated image is the 20th of a 30-frame snippet), right stereo views, GPS coordinates, vehicle odometry and outside temperature. Frames were manually selected in daytime, in good to medium weather, from spring, summer and autumn. Extensions by others add people bounding boxes and fog or rain augmentations, and benchmark suites cover pixel, instance and panoptic labelling and 3D vehicle detection; a 3D dataset was released in August 2020. Access: free but registration is required, and the terms of use limit downloads to people affiliated with scientific bodies. Caveats: it shows street level appearance, not infrastructure attributes, so it suits machine learning for mapping streets and public space, and supports urban digital twin analysis. The terms of use say the scenes come from German, French and Swiss cities; related records are not yet linked.
